subject: wearing outdoor shoes indoors
title: What If You Always Wore Shoes Inside?

scenes.text: What if you always wore your outdoor shoes inside? Your floor becomes everywhere you've walked.
In a University of Arizona test, a brand-new pair picked up four hundred forty thousand units of bacteria in just two weeks.
Shoes worn for three months averaged four hundred twenty-one thousand units, and over a quarter carried E. coli.
Step onto a clean tile floor, and those bacteria transferred over ninety percent of the time.
Germs aren't all. About a third of indoor dust comes from outside, blown or tracked in, including lead from yard soil.
And who lives closest to that floor? One researcher estimates toddlers put their hands in their mouths about eighty times an hour.

description:
What if you always wore shoes inside? University of Arizona researchers found a new pair of shoes picked up about 440,000 units of bacteria in two weeks, shoes worn three months averaged 421,000, 27% carried E. coli, and bacteria transferred to clean tiles more than 90% of the time.
Macquarie University researchers note about a third of indoor dust comes from outside, and that indoor lead is likely linked to yard soil carried in on shoes and pets.
